narrative.overview:
The site reads like the operator touch panel of a modern installation: a graphite ground, soft-cornered tiles sized for a thumb, pill controls, and a state vocabulary so small it reads at a glance. Inside it sit the technician's own field photographs (a cogeneration set, a belt transmission, a sensor, a drive motor, a PLC program, a diagnostic curve), framed in rounded tiles and tagged with equipment codes. What is lit green is what Malo covers or what you can do next. Everything that is not state stays grey.

The panel is calm and tactile rather than square and technical. Sections stack like sheets sliding over one another; cards rise when touched; the header floats as a pill above the page. Colour is never decoration. Motion is the panel coming to life, once: the header drops in, the hero photo opens out of a rounded inset, the headline rises line by line, cards arrive in a short wave, the process line fills green. Nothing loops. It all disappears under reduced motion.

The world refuses the start-up register (neon, glow, gadget effects) and the anonymous trades site (stock photos, icon cards). It is a technician's panel, dark, soft-edged and exact, showing real work.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite ground with four close tonal steps; 1px seams edge every tile.
One-bit state colour: green means running / my domain / live feedback / primary action; amber means urgency or fault. Static facts carry no lamp.
Real field photography only, in rounded tiles, tagged with mono equipment codes on blurred pills.
A role-based radius scale: 10px fields, 16px inner items, 28px tiles (22px on phones), 44px sheets (32px on phones), pills for everything pressed or tagged.
Every touch target is at least 44px tall.
Archivo variable width: compressed caps (66–72% width) for display and titles, 85% for labels, 100% for reading.
JetBrains Mono only for phone numbers, measured values and equipment codes.
One shared lift shadow for what floats or is touched; no other shadows.

rules.name: The One-Bit Rule
rules.body: Green is a state, not a brand accent. It marks what is running, what Malo covers, live system feedback (progress, focus), or the action to take. If an element is none of these, it is grey. A green lamp means running or live; static facts (location, photo captions) never carry one.

rules.name: The Alarm Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where something is urgent or wrong: the emergency line and a fault. Never as a highlight, a category colour, or a second accent.

rules.name: The Grey-Then-Lit Rule
rules.body: Things come on line, they do not arrive coloured: sector stations start Seam and Pipe Grey and light green in sequence; a domain card turns green-edged on Run Tint only when targeted.

rules.name: The Measured Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for what an instrument would print: phone numbers, measured values with units and equipment codes. Never for headings, body, buttons or decoration.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is set by width and weight of the one family, not by a second display face: 66% for display and headlines, 70–72% for titles, 85% for labels, 90% for buttons, 100% for reading. Reading text is never compressed and never set in caps.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Anything you can tap is at least 44px tall: nav links, the menu pill, buttons, the alarm number pill, the direct-line mailto, footer links (50px items in the mobile menu, 54px for the mobile call pill).

rules.name: The Sheet Rule
rules.body: Every section is a sheet: rounded top corners at the sheet radius, a 1px Seam on top, and a negative top margin equal to that radius so it overlaps the previous sheet. Never a flat full-bleed band, never a gap between sections.

rules.name: The Field Photo Rule
rules.body: Only the technician's own field photographs: real equipment on real sites. No stock, no generated or illustrated imagery. Every photo is cropped to remove camera watermarks and carries its origin in the file. Photos are rounded tiles (hero full-height in its tile, domain cards 4:3 inset within the card, about portrait), `object-fit: cover` with a chosen focal point, on a Panel or Ground placeholder. Text on a photo lives only in a pill: Graphite Ground at 82% with a 6–8px backdrop blur, Label type, in a corner.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Touch Rule
rules.body: Tiles rest flat on their seam. Only something that floats over content or responds to the pointer gets the lift, and always the same neutral one. No coloured shadows, no glows.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: A rounded thing inside a rounded thing takes the outer radius minus the inset: a photo inside a domain card is `lg − 8px` (20px, 14px on phones), including the clip-path it unmasks from. Never the same radius inside and out, never square inside round.

rules.name: The Pill-for-Touch Rule
rules.body: If you press it or it labels a state, it is a pill. If it holds content, it is a tile. Only fields take the small 10px corner.

dos: Do build every surface from the four graphite steps (`ground`, `ground-2`, `panel`, `panel-2`) and edge tiles and sheets with a 1px `seam`.

Do pick radius by role: 10px fields, 16px inner items, 28px tiles (22px on phones), 44px sheets (32px on phones), pills for anything pressed or tagged, circles for lamps and stations; always through the tokens so the phone step applies.
Do nest radii: an inset photo takes the card radius minus its inset.
Do use Running Green only for running / covered state, live feedback, focus and the primary action.
Do reserve Alarm Amber, including its tint pills, for the emergency line and for faults.
Do use only the technician's own field photographs, cropped free of camera watermarks, with their origin embedded in the file.
Do put text on photos only inside a blurred Ground pill.
Do set headings and labels in Archivo compressed caps (wdth 66–85) and reading text in Archivo at full width, sentence case.
Do set phone numbers, measured values and equipment codes in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do edge every field and choice with `edge` so its boundary stays at 3:1 or better against its surface.
Do use the single `--lift` shadow, and only for what floats or responds to touch.
Do show everything in place under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep a call action within reach at every scroll position on phones.
Do make every tap target at least 44px tall.
Do mark required fields with "*" and optional ones with "(facultatif)", and put each field's error directly under it.
donts: Don't add coloured shadows, glows or neon, or any shadow other than the lift and the field focus halo.
Don't use green or amber as decoration, category colour or background wash.
Don't use stock photography, generated imagery or illustrations in place of field photos.
Don't use mono for headings, buttons, body or decorative labels.
Don't build icon cards; a domain card opens on a field photo.
Don't put eyebrow labels or kickers above section headings; labels belong to instruments (captions, tags, annunciators).
Don't use typographic glyphs as icons or arrows; draw them as SVG.
Don't mix square corners into the panel, or give an inner element the same radius as its container.
Don't pulse, blink or loop anything; no bounce or spring easing.
Don't put a green lamp on a static fact, or repeat a card's description as chips.
